turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because I just can't stop thinking that the left side of my face looks crooked. It just looks really messed up to me. It's constantly on my mind, and I feel like everyone at the warehouse where I work is noticing it. Even when I try to do things I enjoy, like going to salsa night, I just know people are staring at it. They tell me they don't see anything wrong when I ask, but... I just can't shake it. It's really getting to me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports a persistent preoccupation with a perceived defect in their facial symmetry that others state they do not see.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself checking your face in mirrors, taking photos of it, or asking others repeatedly if they notice anything wrong with how it looks?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. At work, especially. Like... before I go back out on the inventory floor, I just keep checking my face in the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my cap, trying to see how it looks, and just rubbing at that same spot on my face over and over. 

It gets pretty bad because sometimes I'm in there so long that I'm late getting back out to my section. My picking numbers fall behind because of it, and my boss has been getting on me again about my times. So, yeah, I do check it a lot.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors related to their appearance, specifically repeatedly checking their face in the mirror, adjusting their cap, and rubbing a spot on their face to the point of workplace impairment.

turns.doctor_question: Besides the way your face looks, do you experience any physical sensations in that area—like pain, tingling, numbness, or weakness?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't feel anything like that. It doesn't hurt or tingle or anything. It feels totally normal... it's just the way it looks that's the problem.
